points.html: The Maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is fixed at 250. In addition to the prior two conditions, he must be an elector for a parliamentary constituency in India. *The Vice-President of India is the ex- officio chairman of the Council of States/Upper House of Parliament. *When the Vice-President acts as the President he shall not be entitled to get the salary and allowances of the Chairman of Rajya Sabha. For this period, he receives salary and allowances of the President. *Rajya Sabha elects a deputy chairman from amongst its members. *The Deputy Chairman gives his resignation in writing to the Chairman. *Rajya Sabha has the power to remove the Deputy Chairman from his post, by a resolution passed by the absolute majority of the total members of Rajya Sabha. Such resolution can be moved only after giving at least 14 days' notice. *When the post of Chairman is vacant, the deputy chairman will perform the duties of the chairman. *While presiding over the Rajya Sabha, the Deputy Chairman can't vote in general, he can only exercise a casting vote in case of a tie. *When a resolution to remove the Vice- President from his office is under consideration, he will not be presiding as the Chairman and when a resolution of removal of the Deputy Chairman is under consideration, he will not be presiding as the Deputy Chairman. *The representation of states in Rajya Sabha is given in proportion to their population. *For a quorum, there must be the presence of one-tenth of the total number of members in the Rajya Sabha. *The Representation of People Act 1951 (through an amendment in 2003) made a provision that any person can contest from anywhere for Rajya Sabha even if he is a resident of any other state. Now for contesting Rajya Sabha elections, a person must be an elector in a parliamentary constituency anywhere in India. *The 4th Schedule of the Indian Constitution enumerates the allocation of Rajya Sabha seats for states and union territories. *Article 249 states that if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution with a 2/3 majority of its members present and voting, the Parliament can make laws in the national interest regarding the subjects of the state list, which are specified in the resolution. *It is valid for a period of 1 year, but it can be extended by passing a resolution.
